newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico PRI ahead in Campeche governor's race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexico PRI ahead in Campeche governor's race - poll.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) is leading both main opposition parties in July's race to win the governorship of Mexico's Campeche state, the newspaper Reforma reported on Tuesday.

Reforma said its own poll in the state gave the PRI 41 percent, compared to 29 percent for the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) and two percent for the conservative National Action Party (PAN).

Campeche is one of Mexico's less important states but the PRD had high hopes of winning its first governorship there after fielding as its candidate Layda Sansores, a senator and former governor's daughter who defected from the PRI last year.

Campeche is one of six states choosing a governor in the July elections. Polls so far have put the PRI ahead in all but one state, Nuevo Leon, where the race is too tight to call between the PRI and the PAN.
The PRD however leads most polls in the race for the first elected mayor of Mexico City, who will also be chosen on July 6.

Twenty-three percent of the 821 people surveyed by Reforma in Campeche were unsure of their preference and five percent said they would back the left-wing Workers Party. The poll was conducted between April 11-25 and had a margin of error of 3.5 percent.
